items.title: Clarence "Little Dad" Vincent Interview, 1960-01-21
items.q: I played with him about three years. But it wasn't his band, it was Lewis the Man's band.

ctx.x: When you were about 12 years old, you have here on the sheet. A sheet of paper. What about August Roussel?

What about August Roussel? August Roussel used to play with us too. He was a tambour player. He was a good leader too, but sometimes he used to make mistakes and Lewis the Man, he used to get after him all the time, you know. I played with him about three years. But it wasn't his band, it was Lewis the Man's band. And we had Gus Muscapper and Robert Hall. You heard talking about Robert Hall? Edward Hall's brother. We had a line up like that. We had Henry Rush with us once. When he quit, we had Joe Stratton. You…
Slide whistle, you mean? Yeah. And Henry Rush was playing drums at the time?

items.title: Clarence "Little Dad" Vincent Interview, 1959-12-03
items.q: And Lewis Tameen had me with him then.

ctx.x: And ask him if you ever worked with the Young Morgan Band.

Have you ever worked with the Young Morgan Band? Yeah, yeah. Let me see. Isaiah Martin. Yeah, I used to work with him. He played his band. He played for me. He was playing out at Spanish Post. And you know, old man, Transcena, he could play music too. Transcena, that's the fella who used to run the place out there, you know. You know what I was talking about? Transcena? That was the boss, you know, who used to run that, you know, that place out there. But anyhow, he was a great bass fella. He didn't sit in the…
When did you start using ninths? Who? When did you start using- Using ninths?

items.title: Clarence "Little Dad" Vincent Interview, 1959-11-17
items.q: Let me see when that was. Twenty-something years ago, I think. We used to play with the same band, Gus Muscat.

ctx.x: When did you play with Dumaine? Let me see when that was. Twenty-something years ago, I think. We used to play with the same band, Gus Muscat. Now let's figure out how else about him. Gus Muscat. He was a baratone man.
